Measured 2026-10-31T21:17:34 on Windows-11-10.0.26300-SP0, Python 3.12.10, 30 runs per row, warm OS cache, `--offline`. Command:

    python bench/bench.py --runs 30 --compare bench/baseline.json --markdown docs/PERF.md --json bench/latest.json

Scenarios: A = 1 file / 20 lines; B = 20 files / 400 lines (Python + JS); C = 300-file change; D = the A change in a 50,000-file repo. A-D run with the defaults (result cache off). `-cold` rows add `--no-cache`; `-cache` rows add `--cache` (result cache on, filled by a first run). `startup-hook` is `--version` started the way POSIX hooks start the gate (reusing its bytecode); it is not measured on Windows, where hooks run the script directly. `python -c pass` is the interpreter's own start-up on the same machine.

Baseline: v0.1.0 measured 2026-10-31T16:38:24 on the same machine (`bench/baseline.json`).

Most of the baseline's time went to `importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` scanning every package installed in the interpreter, which v0.1.0 ran on every check. The large gains over the baseline therefore depend on the environment: with few installed packages the baseline, and the gain, are much smaller. Compare rows within one run for anything else.
